title: Nepal Travel Guide
summary: Practical information for planning a trip to Nepal.

topics.title: Nepal Tourist Visa Information
topics.summary: How to get a Nepal tourist visa on arrival, at an embassy or online, with durations and fees.
intro: **Nepal tourist visas are available on arrival at the Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu, or at border entry points in Kakadvitta, Birgunj, Bhairahawa, Nepalgunj, Gaddachowki on the Nepal-India border, and Kodari and Kerung on the Nepal-China border.**

**A Nepal tourist visa is also available at the nearest Nepal Embassy or diplomatic mission for Nepal in your country.** A visa can also be obtained (for renewal purposes) at the Department of Immigration, Kalikasthan, Kathmandu. A valid passport and one passport-size photo with a light background are required.

**Visa is available only through payment in cash of the currency of Euro, Swiss Franc, Pound Sterling, US Dollar, Australian Dollar, Canadian Dollar, Hong Kong Dollar, Singapore Dollar, and Japanese Yen.** Credit cards, Indian currency, and Nepali rupees are not accepted to pay the visa fee.

sections.heading: Nepal Tourist Visa Duration and Fees
bullets: Multiple entry 15 days US$ 30 or equivalent convertible currency
Multiple entries 30 days US$ 50 or equivalent convertible currency
Multiple entries 90 days US$ 125 or equivalent convertible currency

sections.heading: Gratis (Free) Visa
paragraphs: **For the first visit in one visa year (January to December), a 30-day gratis visa is available only for nationals of South Asian countries like Bangladesh, Bhutan, Maldives, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka.** However, the visa is extendable from the Immigration Department upon payment of the visa fee as specified above.
sections.note: **Note: Indian nationals do not require a visa to enter Nepal.**

sections.heading: For Indian National
bullets: Indian nationals do not require a visa to enter Nepal.
As per the Nepalese Immigration, Indian Nationals Traveling to Nepal must possess the following documents.
Passport
Driving License with photo
Photo Identity card issued by a Government Agency
Election Commission Card with Photo
Identity Card issued by the Embassy of India in Kathmandu
Identity Card with Photo issued by Sub- Sub-Divisional Magistrate or any other officials above his rank

sections.heading: Nepal Tourist Visa Online Application
bullets: You can now apply for a Nepal Tourism Visa online. Please visit the online visa page to apply.
Nepal Visa Online Apply: **http://online.nepalimmigration.gov.np/tourist-visa**

sections.note: **Note: Fees and rules change from time to time. Please confirm the latest details with us or the official authority before you travel.**

topics.title: Nepal Travel Insurance
topics.summary: Why trekkers need insurance with helicopter evacuation and what the policy should cover.
intro: **Travel insurance is mandatory for all our trekking and expedition trips in Nepal.** Treks go to high altitude in remote areas, where a rescue is usually only possible by helicopter and a hospital can be days away on foot.
**Please buy your insurance before you travel and carry a copy of the policy and the emergency contact number with you.** We will ask for the policy details before your trip starts.

sections.heading: What the Policy Should Cover
bullets: Emergency helicopter evacuation and rescue from high altitude
Medical treatment and hospital expenses, including altitude sickness
Trekking up to the maximum altitude of your itinerary (many standard policies stop at 3,000 to 4,000 meters)
Trip cancellation and interruption
Lost, stolen or delayed baggage and personal belongings
Repatriation to your home country

sections.heading: Before You Buy
bullets: Tell the insurer the exact trek and the highest altitude you will reach
Check that adventure activities such as trekking, peak climbing or rafting are not excluded
Ask whether the insurer pays the rescue company directly or you must pay first and claim later
Keep the policy number and the 24-hour emergency phone number with your passport

sections.heading: If You Need a Rescue
paragraphs: Tell your guide immediately. Your guide will contact the rescue company and your insurer, and we will help with the paperwork. A helicopter rescue is only possible in suitable weather and is arranged once the insurer has confirmed cover, so having the policy details ready saves valuable time.

topics.title: Trekking Permits and Fees
topics.summary: The permits, national park fees and local area charges for Nepal's trekking regions.
intro: **Most treks in Nepal require a national park or conservation area permit together with a local municipality fee.** Restricted regions such as Upper Mustang, Manaslu and Dolpo need a special permit and can only be trekked with a registered trekking agency and a licensed guide.
**We arrange every permit and entry fee for your trek and include them in the trip cost,** so you do not have to queue at the offices in Kathmandu or Pokhara.

sections.heading: Common Trekking Permits
bullets: Sagarmatha National Park entry permit and Khumbu local municipality permit: Everest region treks
Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP): Annapurna Circuit, Annapurna Base Camp and Poon Hill
Langtang National Park permit: Langtang Valley and Gosainkunda
Manaslu Conservation Area Permit and Annapurna Conservation Area Permit: Manaslu Circuit
Restricted Area Permit: Upper Mustang, Manaslu, Upper Dolpo, Nar Phu and Kanchenjunga

sections.heading: Restricted Area Rules
bullets: At least two trekkers are required for most restricted areas
A licensed guide from a registered agency must accompany you
Permits are issued by the Department of Immigration and you need a valid visa and passport copy
Permit prices depend on the area, the season and the number of days

sections.heading: What We Need From You
bullets: Clear scan of your passport and visa pages
Two passport-size photos
Your arrival and departure dates
Your insurance details

sections.note: **Note: Fees and rules change from time to time. Please confirm the latest details with us or the official authority before you travel.**

topics.title: Sightseeing Entry Fees in Nepal
topics.summary: Entry fees for the heritage sites and national parks you will visit on a Nepal tour.
intro: **The heritage squares of Kathmandu Valley, the main temples and the national parks charge separate entry fees for foreign visitors.** SAARC nationals pay a lower rate and children are often free or discounted.

**Carry your passport or a copy,** since some ticket counters ask for proof of nationality. Entry fees are usually included in our guided tour packages, and the trip inclusions list shows exactly which ones.

sections.heading: Kathmandu Valley Heritage Sites
bullets: Kathmandu Durbar Square
Patan Durbar Square
Bhaktapur Durbar Square
Swayambhunath Stupa (Monkey Temple)
Boudhanath Stupa
Pashupatinath Temple area
Changu Narayan Temple

sections.heading: National Parks and Other Sites
bullets: Chitwan National Park: jungle safari
Lumbini, the birthplace of Lord Buddha
Bardia National Park
Pokhara attractions such as the International Mountain Museum and Davis Falls

sections.heading: Good to Know
bullets: Tickets are valid for one day at most sites, and the date is stamped on them
Some temples, including parts of Pashupatinath, are open to Hindus only
Photography rules differ from site to site, so ask your guide
Dress modestly when visiting temples and monasteries

sections.note: **Note: Fees and rules change from time to time. Please confirm the latest details with us or the official authority before you travel.**

topics.title: Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS) in Nepal
topics.summary: Symptoms, prevention and treatment of altitude sickness on Himalayan treks.
intro: **Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS) is caused by climbing too fast to high altitude, and it can affect anyone regardless of age or fitness.** Early symptoms usually begin from about 2,500 to 3,000 meters.
**Most cases are mild and go away with rest and a slower pace,** but AMS can become life-threatening if you ignore it and keep climbing.

sections.heading: Symptoms of Mild AMS
bullets: Headache
Nausea, dizziness and loss of appetite
Poor sleep and unusual tiredness
Shortness of breath on exertion

sections.heading: Danger Signs
paragraphs: **Confusion, loss of balance, breathlessness at rest, a wet cough or a worsening headache mean the condition is serious.** These can be signs of high altitude cerebral or pulmonary edema, and the only safe treatment is an immediate descent.
sections.note: **Note: Never go higher with AMS symptoms, and never leave a sick person to descend alone.**

sections.heading: How to Prevent AMS
bullets: Ascend gradually and follow the acclimatization days in your itinerary
"Climb high, sleep low": a short walk higher in the day helps your body adapt
Drink three to four liters of water every day
Avoid alcohol and smoking at altitude
Eat well even if your appetite is low
Tell your guide about any symptom early

sections.heading: Treatment
bullets: Mild AMS: rest where you are until symptoms go away before going higher
Symptoms that get worse: descend at once, even at night
Severe cases: emergency evacuation by helicopter, which your insurance should cover
Ask your doctor before the trip about altitude medicine such as acetazolamide

topics.title: Drone Regulations in Nepal
topics.summary: Permissions you need before flying a drone in Nepal.
intro: **Flying a drone in Nepal requires permission from the authorities, and the rules are strictly enforced.** National parks, conservation areas and heritage sites have their own regulations in addition to national rules.
**Please tell us before you travel if you plan to bring a drone.** Customs can hold an undeclared drone at the airport, and flying without permission can lead to a fine or confiscation.

sections.heading: Before You Fly
bullets: Get permission from the Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal (CAAN) for the area you plan to fly
Get separate permission from the national park or conservation area office where required
Declare the drone at customs when you arrive in Kathmandu
Carry copies of your permits while flying

sections.heading: Restricted Places
bullets: Near airports and in the airspace of Kathmandu Valley
Over government buildings, security areas and borders
Over temples, monasteries and religious ceremonies
In many protected areas without a special permit

sections.heading: Flying Responsibly
bullets: Keep the drone in your line of sight and away from people and wildlife
Respect privacy and local customs
Do not fly in bad weather or in strong mountain winds

title: Bhutan Travel Guide
summary: Practical information for planning a trip to Bhutan.

topics.title: Bhutan Tourist Visa Information
topics.summary: How Bhutan visas are arranged and what the daily Sustainable Development Fee covers.
intro: **All visitors to Bhutan, except nationals of India, Bangladesh and the Maldives, need a visa.** The visa is applied for online through a licensed Bhutanese tour operator or the official tourism portal before you travel.
**The visa is processed once your trip is booked and the payment is received.** You get a visa clearance letter by email, and the visa is stamped in your passport when you arrive in Bhutan.

sections.heading: What You Need
bullets: A passport valid for at least six months from the date of arrival
A passport-size digital photo
Confirmed travel dates and itinerary
Payment of the visa fee and the Sustainable Development Fee

sections.heading: Sustainable Development Fee
paragraphs: **Visitors pay a Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) for every night spent in Bhutan,** which supports free education and healthcare, conservation and infrastructure. Children are charged at a reduced rate and very young children are exempt.

sections.heading: Indian, Bangladeshi and Maldivian Visitors
bullets: Indian nationals can enter with a passport or voter ID card and need an entry permit
Bangladeshi and Maldivian nationals do not need a visa but follow their own fee rules

sections.note: **Note: Fees and rules change from time to time. Please confirm the latest details with us or the official authority before you travel.**

topics.title: Bhutan Travel Insurance
topics.summary: Cover to arrange before you travel to Bhutan.
intro: **Medical facilities in Bhutan are limited outside Thimphu and Paro,** and treks and mountain roads can be far from a hospital. We strongly recommend comprehensive travel insurance for every visitor.

sections.heading: What the Policy Should Cover
bullets: Medical treatment and hospital expenses
Emergency evacuation, including by helicopter
Trekking at altitude if you plan to hike, such as the Druk Path Trek
Trip cancellation and interruption
Lost or delayed baggage and personal belongings

sections.heading: Tips
bullets: Buy the insurance when you book, so cancellations are covered
Keep the policy number and the emergency phone number with your passport
Tell your guide about any medical condition or medicine you take

topics.title: Best Time to Visit Bhutan
topics.summary: Seasons, festivals and weather month by month.
intro: **The best seasons to visit Bhutan are spring (March to May) and autumn (September to November),** when the skies are clear, temperatures are comfortable and most festivals take place.

sections.heading: Spring (March to May)
bullets: Rhododendrons and wildflowers bloom in the valleys and on the hills
The Paro Tshechu festival is usually held in spring
Warm days and good mountain views, with some rain in May

sections.heading: Summer (June to August)
bullets: Monsoon rain brings green landscapes but muddy trails and some road delays
Fewer visitors and a quieter experience

sections.heading: Autumn (September to November)
bullets: Clear skies and the best Himalayan views
The Thimphu Tshechu and other major festivals
The best season for trekking

sections.heading: Winter (December to February)
bullets: Cold at altitude but sunny in the valleys
Black-necked cranes visit the Phobjikha Valley
Few visitors and some high passes may be closed by snow

topics.title: Altitude and Health in Bhutan
topics.summary: What to know about altitude and staying healthy in Bhutan.
intro: **Paro is at about 2,200 meters and Thimphu at about 2,300 meters,** and the Tiger's Nest hike and the passes on the Druk Path Trek go much higher. Most visitors feel fine, but altitude affects everyone differently.

sections.heading: Staying Healthy
bullets: Walk slowly and take rests on the first day after you arrive
Drink plenty of water and avoid too much alcohol
Use sun protection, since the sun is strong at altitude
Carry any regular medicine and a basic first-aid kit
Drink bottled or boiled water only

sections.heading: If You Feel Unwell
paragraphs: Tell your guide about a headache, nausea or breathlessness early. Mild symptoms usually pass with rest, and your guide can change the day's plan or arrange a descent if needed.

title: Tibet Travel Guide
summary: Practical information for planning a trip to Tibet.

topics.title: Tibet Travel Permit
topics.summary: The permits required to enter and travel inside Tibet.
intro: **Foreign visitors must have a Tibet Travel Permit to enter Tibet, and it can only be arranged by a licensed tour operator.** You cannot apply for it yourself, and independent travel is not allowed.
**Some areas need extra permits,** and your operator arranges them together with your itinerary.

sections.heading: Permits You May Need
bullets: Tibet Travel Permit (TTB permit) for entering Tibet
Alien's Travel Permit for areas outside Lhasa
Military or border permit for Everest Base Camp, Mount Kailash and other border areas

sections.heading: What We Need From You
bullets: Clear scan of your passport
Your Chinese visa copy, or your Nepal passport details if you apply in Kathmandu
Your occupation and travel dates

sections.heading: Timing
paragraphs: Permits take time to process and cannot be issued without a confirmed itinerary, so please book several weeks before you travel. Permit rules can change at short notice, especially around festivals and national holidays.

sections.note: **Note: Fees and rules change from time to time. Please confirm the latest details with us or the official authority before you travel.**

topics.title: China Visa for Tibet
topics.summary: How to get a Chinese visa when you enter Tibet from Nepal or from mainland China.
intro: **If you enter Tibet from Kathmandu, you need a Chinese group visa issued in Kathmandu by the Chinese embassy,** arranged for you by your tour operator after your Tibet Travel Permit is approved.
**If you arrive from mainland China, you use your regular Chinese visa,** and your operator arranges the Tibet Travel Permit separately.

sections.heading: Entering From Nepal
bullets: Do not get a Chinese visa from your home country: it is not valid for a Tibet entry from Nepal
Your Chinese group visa is a separate paper, not stuck in your passport
You collect the visa in Kathmandu, usually two to three working days after you submit your passport
The visa is valid only for the group trip and the dates in your itinerary

sections.heading: Keep in Mind
bullets: Plan a few days in Kathmandu for the visa before you cross into Tibet
Visa dates and fees can change, so rely on your operator for current details
Your passport must have blank pages and at least six months' validity

sections.note: **Note: Fees and rules change from time to time. Please confirm the latest details with us or the official authority before you travel.**

topics.title: Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS) in Tibet
topics.summary: Staying safe on the high Tibetan plateau.
intro: **Lhasa is at 3,650 meters and most Tibetan sights are higher still,** with Everest Base Camp at about 5,200 meters and Mount Kailash at about 4,700 meters. You arrive at altitude quickly, so acclimatization matters.

sections.heading: Common Symptoms
bullets: Headache, dizziness and nausea
Poor sleep and loss of appetite
Shortness of breath, even at rest in severe cases

sections.heading: How to Reduce the Risk
bullets: Take it easy on your first day in Lhasa and avoid hot showers and heavy meals
Drink plenty of water and avoid alcohol
Climb gradually and follow the schedule in your itinerary
Tell your guide about any symptom early
Ask your doctor about altitude medicine before you travel
sections.note: **Note: Descend immediately if symptoms get worse. Vehicles carry oxygen on most routes.**

topics.title: Best Time to Visit Tibet
topics.summary: Seasons, weather and road access across the year.
intro: **The main travel season in Tibet is April to October,** when the weather is milder and the mountain roads are open. Winters are very cold but quiet.

sections.heading: Spring (April to May)
bullets: Clear skies and fewer visitors than in summer
Everest Base Camp opens for the season
Cold nights, so pack warm clothing

sections.heading: Summer (June to August)
bullets: Warm days and green valleys, with some rain
Peak season for crowds and the Shoton festival in Lhasa
Mount Kailash pilgrimage season runs from about May to September

sections.heading: Autumn (September to October)
bullets: Crisp, clear weather and good mountain views
A good time for photography

sections.heading: Winter (November to March)
bullets: Very cold, with some remote areas closed
Fewer visitors and lower hotel prices in Lhasa
